title: Calendula cold-process soap
subtitle: A gentle bar for babies, eczema-prone, and sensitive skin
excerpt: A cold-process bar made with calendula-infused olive oil and dried calendula petals in the batter, giving a yellow-gold tone and the mild, skin-kind character of the flower. No synthetic fragrance. Makes 7 bars.
sourceNotes: Calendula officinalis in soap and cosmetics: EMA HMPC monograph (2008). Calendula-infused oil in cold-process soap: general soapmaking reference. Note: the alkaline saponification process may reduce some of the plant actives from the infused oil; the main benefit is the oil's fatty acid profile and the visual petals in the bar. SAP value for calendula-infused sunflower/olive oil base: approximately 0.134 (treat as olive oil for calculation). Dried calendula petals: they turn brown in the alkaline bar after a few weeks of cure; this is expected.

recipe.batchNotes: Run any scale change through a lye calculator.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a cool dark cupboard once cured. The calendula petals will brown over the cure period; this does not affect the bar's quality. Discard if DOS or a rancid smell appear.

glossaryTerms.definition: The reaction between fat and sodium hydroxide that produces soap and glycerine. Each oil has a SAP value: grams of lye per gram of oil.
The point at which soap batter thickens to thin-custard consistency. The signal to pour.

A carrier oil in which dried plant material has been steeped to extract the plant's beneficial compounds. Calendula-infused olive oil is made by steeping dried calendula flowers in olive oil for four to six weeks.

projectSchedule.title: Unmould and cut
projectSchedule.body: Turn out the loaf. The bar will be a warm yellow-gold from the calendula infusion with orange-gold petal flecks in the cut face.

projectSchedule.title: Turn the bars
projectSchedule.body: Flip each bar. The petal colour will begin to brown in the alkaline bar; this is expected.

projectSchedule.title: Four-week test
projectSchedule.body: Test a sliver. No sting means safe to use. The bar is suitable for sensitive skin from this point.

projectSchedule.title: Cure complete
projectSchedule.body: A fully cured calendula bar is firm, golden, and very mild. The lather is gentle and creamy.

content.text: Note: the dried calendula petals are decorative only and are stirred in at trace rather than listed as a measured ingredient. Use 1 to 2 tablespoons loose-packed. Lavender essential oil is listed as optional; omit it for a fully unscented bar.
In a ventilated space with protective gloves and goggles on, add the sodium hydroxide to the distilled water. Stir until dissolved. Cool to 38 to 42°C.
Melt the coconut oil and shea butter. Add the calendula-infused oil and castor oil. Cool to 38 to 42°C.
Pour the lye solution into the oils. Blend to trace. Stir in one to two tablespoons of dried calendula petals by hand. Pour into the silicone mould.
Wrap in a towel. Leave 48 hours. Unmould wearing protective gloves. Cut and cure 4 to 6 weeks. The petal colours will brown during cure; this does not affect quality.
Two years in a cool dark cupboard. Discard if DOS or rancid smell appear.
